summary: First-token latency spike for interactive chat after quantized-shard migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (TextFlow Labs, Dedicated cluster) are observing a large increase in time-to-first-token (TTFT) for interactive chat completions after the recent quantized-shard migration performed during the 2026-03-12 runtime deployment window. The problem manifests as ~800ms to 3s extra latency on initial token emission for many short prompt sessions. Subsequent token streaming appears normal once generation begins.

Impact:
- Multiple customers on Dedicated pools report degraded UX for chat features (slow initial response).
- Error budgets affected for low-latency SLAs; some sessions timeout at the application layer when combined with client-side 2s handshake timeouts.

Timeline / Observed events:
- 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC: Quantized shard migration roll-out started for runtime-2.5 -> runtime-2.6 on dedicated pools (deploy PR #542).
- 2026-03-12 22:15 UTC: Automated rollout completed for ~60% of dedicated nodes in us-east and eu-west.
- 2026-03-12 22:40 UTC: First customer report (internal slack #support) of increased first-token latency for short-chat flows.
- 2026-03-12 23:00 UTC: Support ticket opened by TextFlow Labs.

Environment / Config:
- Dedicated GPU pools (p4d/p100-equivalent allocation), runtime-2.6 (quantized-shard enabled), autoscaling ON, routing policy: latency-preferred with fallback to cheaper quant variants.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions (streaming enabled).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Create a short chat session with 1-2 user messages (<= 40 tokens).
2) Call /v1/chat/completions with stream=true and max_tokens=128.
3) Observe response: long delay before first chunk arrives; subsequent streaming tokens at expected rates.

Observed behavior:
- Median first-token latency increased from ~120ms to ~1.1s for short prompts; 95th percentiles up to 3s.
- No increase in 5xx spike correlated with these sessions.
- Request traces show increased time spent in "kv-cache-load" and "shard-layout-resolve" phases prior to decode.

Expected behavior:
- First token emitted within previous baseline (~<200ms) for warm nodes and modestly higher for cold.

Customer logs / sample request IDs:
- Request IDs (sample): rq_us_east_20260312_01: 7c2b8a1f, 7c2b8a3c, 7c2b8a8f
- Traces (shortened): 
  - 7c2b8a1f: queue_wait=18ms, proxy_auth=4ms, shard-assign=32ms, kv-cache-load=860ms, decode-init=10ms, first-token=950ms
  - 7c2b8a8f: queue_wait=12ms, shard-assign=28ms, kv-cache-load=2200ms, decode-init=12ms, first-token=2246ms

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Pin to runtime-2.5 (pre-migration) via model pinning for affected route — mitigates first-token lag but not a long-term solution.
- Toggle routing policy to prefer non-quantized variant for latency-sensitive routes until fix deployed.

Additional notes:
- This seems focused on short prompts where prefix/KV cache lookup dominates per-request cost. Long-running generation sessions do not show user-visible regression after the initial load.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: quantized-shard layout change introduced synchronous cold-loading of per-shard metadata (shard-index + mmap page population) on request path for small inputs. SRE reproduced increased kv-cache-load latency in staging when forcing cold page faults for quantized models.

What we've checked so far:
- Instrumented runtime (local staging) with shard warm/unwarm toggles; observed >1.5s extra on first request when shard tables unloaded.
- Verified scheduler and autoscaler not queuing an unusual number of requests at observed times.
- No correlating increase in 5xx or OOMs.
- Kernel-level dmesg shows occasional page-in batches at migration windows on older kernels (p4d host images) but inconsistent.
- Related PR (#542) introduced new shard index file format and cache population on model load.

Open actions:
- (ENG-1) Add background population task at model-load time to warm shard metadata off the request-critical path. Owner: Jonah Kim. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- (ENG-2) Backfill warm cache job for affected dedicated pools and run a rolling pre-warm during low-traffic windows. Owner: infra-ops. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- (SRE-1) Add temporary routing rule to prefer runtime-2.5 for routes tagged latency-sensitive for TextFlow Labs while hotfix is prepared. Owner: SRE oncall. ETA: immediate.

2026-03-12 23:30 Jonah Kim (SRE): Reproduced elevated first-token latency in staging by simulating cold shard state. Initial suspicion: cache population on request path due to new shard format. Linking runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/abc123def

2026-03-13 02:10 Elena Garcia (Platform Eng): Running kernel and host-image audit to see if page-fault patterns line up with migration. Found intermittent madvise/pagein spikes on older host images (p4d-ami-2025.11) — possible contributing factor.

2026-03-14 08:20 Jonah Kim (SRE): Drafted hotfix to move shard metadata population to model-load background worker and submitted PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/578. Requesting code review and load test.

2026-03-14 11:00 TextFlow Labs (customer): Confirmed that after pinning to runtime-2.5 latency returned to baseline. Asking for ETA on permanent fix and whether backfill will be scheduled for their pool.
resolution: Mitigation performed: route pinned to runtime-2.5 for affected customer and temporary routing rule added to prefer non-quantized model variants for latency-sensitive routes. Engineering implemented background shard-warm worker (PR #578) and scheduled a rolling backfill to pre-populate per-shard metadata across dedicated nodes. Hotfix landed to staging 2026-03-14; full rollout planned after load tests (ETA 2026-03-16). Follow-ups: monitor TTFB metrics for two business-days and coordinate with customer for pool pre-warm window. Marking ticket resolved once rollout completes and metrics confirm baseline recovery.

notes_for_postmortem: Root cause likely multi-factor: upstream change to shard index format + synchronous metadata population + some older host images causing slower page-in behavior. Action item: add explicit pre-warm step in migration playbook and include host-image compatibility check for page-in behaviour. Include a checklist item to run a 'cold-boot' synthetic test targeting short prompts prior to broad rollout.
